Self-flying drones were a hot topic of discussion at the 16th World Knowledge Forum hosted by the Maeil Business Newspaper last month, with experts presenting mixed views on the growth outlook of the drone industry.
At the forum, Teal Group Corporation, a United States-based defense industry consulting firm, forecast the global drone market to reach $10 billion in 2020.
Sales posted by China’s DJI, the world’s largest drone manufacturer, reached $500 million last year, increasing by a hundredfold in three years.
“DJI’s sales will likely reach over $1 billion this year,” said Yoon Kwang-joon, professor of engineering at Konkuk University.
But he added it is required to hone precision landing system of drones and computer operating technology for third-generation drones.

Ben Chung, center manager and program leader at Cisco’s Global Center of Excellence, also said we should prepare a more connected world in which drones integrated with the Internet of Things (IoT) devices would allow people to live.
As we live in a society where billions of devices are inter-connected, it is important to learn how we should deal with the data that is formed by connected devices, Chung added.

Song Yong-kyu, professor at Korea Aerospace University, said that the U.S. focuses on developing unmanned air combat fighter jets to minimize war damages, such as pilot losses. “The South Korean Air Force should be prepared too,” he urged.

Jason Pontin, editor in chief and publisher of MIT Technology Review, however, gave a different view about drones, saying that there is a lot of bubble in the drones industry. “Amazon has envisioned that drones will be widely used in future delivery services, however, I disagree,” Pontin said.
He added that there needs to be a more realistic explanation on how the drone industry is actually formed and refuted the claim that about 300 billion drones will fly around in 2035.
